What our parents say about us
Parent Survey 2025
Please see the wonderful comments parents, carers and visitors share with us:
I thought I would write to thank you and all the staff at the school for making my grandson’s first experience of school such a positive and rewarding one, with a special thanks of course to Mrs Butler. I asked my grandson today how he was finding school. His response was ‘I love it’. This was said with great gusto (understatement). I then asked what especially did he like about school - his response, again said extremely enthusiastically, was ‘absolutely everything!!’. I cannot think of a greater compliment about your school, teachers and staff than that! Thank you so much for all of your hard work and it is much appreciated - a happier bunch of children going into school would be hard to find. September 2024
In a time when people are very quick to complain, I wanted to just let you know how pleased we are with the boys’ experience at Roundwood; the school has educated, supported and nurtured them exceptionally this year. July 2024
A great school in which my child is thriving. He enjoys learning but most of all he is happy to go to school everyday. July 2024
Will be a shame when my child leaves in July because I know that he has really enjoyed Roundwood. The caring ethos of the school shines through and I particularly love the emphasis that has been placed on personal development. The pupil passport is a fantastic initiative - and it's a shame my son wasn't in an earlier year group. School is not just about the curriculum - and Roundwood has succeeded in bringing out the best in children. Roundwood and all the staff - you will be missed! July 2024
We are very happy with the school and the teachers have been nothing but supportive. We feel that our daughter is thriving here, lots of opportunities outside the subjects. July 2024
We love the school! July 2024
The communication between staff and parents has been exceptional July 2024
My child really enjoys going to school and is able to share how she feels with her teachers and school staff. I feel informed about what she is learning and I feel there is good communication between school and home. July 2024
I just wanted to send a note to say thank you for another great sports day at Gawcott yesterday. Another successful event! It was great to see the children, and staff team, having so much fun. Also, the children did such a great job of cheering each other on. So nice to see such positivity. June 2024
I just wanted to pass our huge thanks to the school, Mrs Kent and everyone that helped with making the children's Longridge residential trip so special. Our daughter had a fantastic time and speaking with some of the other parents it sounds like they all thoroughly enjoyed themselves. I hope that the teachers and staff that looked after our children will be enjoying a well earned weekend break. Thank you for making such special memories for the children. May 2024
I just wanted to say how enormously grateful we are to you all for making our daughter's first residential school trip so wonderful. She had the best time. As a parent, I so appreciated the constant communication with updates and photos. And when problems arose (I forgot bunny AND the wash bag!) these were resolved with care and understanding, going above and beyond to make her feel at ease. I truly appreciate it. . Wishing you all a restful weekend! May 2024
I am writing to express our families thanks for your organisation of the Echoes event. This has been an unbelievably great experience for our children and that would not have happened without the support you provided. It must have been an exceptionally long day for you which would have meant a prolonged period away from your own homes and families whilst supporting our children; not to mention having to go into school first thing the next day. We are genuinely thankful that you provide such rich learning experiences for our children. Thank you for being so great! April 2024
An email to say thank you to the staff for making the choir trip to the Royal Albert Hall so special for our son. It is one he will remember for a long long time and so will we. It was incredible to watch, so proud of Roundwood, but a special thank you for instilling an inspiration in him with regards to his piano playing, in an orchestra, and seeing this from a back stage perspective. He has had the best day and thank you for looking after him so well. April 2024
Just a very quick note from me to share some positive feedback. The phonics QR codes that Mrs Field sent him with Y1 this week is such a clever idea. I just wanted to say I thought it was great. As is the online parents evening booking and online permission slips etc. April 2024
Just wanted to pop an email and say that was such a lovely idea for Easter celebrations! We thoroughly enjoyed it and looked like everyone else did too so thank you!
Hope you all have a lovely Easter break, you deserve it. March 2024
I have just spent a lovely afternoon at Roundwood. I was made to feel very welcome, I had a little tour of the school and was offered some delicious school made cakes, but the real highlight of my afternoon was watching the year 3 and 4 Easter production You Are Special. It was a really special event. March 2024
I love that this world book day the children were asked to be in their PJs. Inclusive and focusing on the book. Thank you. March 2024

Wraparound care - S4A
At Roundwood Primary School, we are proud to work in partnership with Sports 4 All (S4A) who deliver both our PE and games curriculum, and our wraparound care.
Wraparound care consists of breakfast club and after school club. Breakfast club runs from each site at 7:30am, whilst after school club runs from 3pm onwards at both sites too.
S4A strive to create a childcare environment that allows children to pursue their interests through a wide variety of exciting activities. They play a huge part in children’s development, helping them to become creative and open minded by providing inspiring role models and high quality provision. S4A are Ofsted accredited so you can ensure that children get the highest level of childcare in a safe and secure environment, giving you peace of mind.
For information on times and prices along with how to book, please visit the link below:

Personal Development
At Roundwood Primary school each pupil has a personal development passport. The personal development passport is full of activities, experiences and events that children will work towards and achieve over the year.
See how the passport progresses through each year group:
Why have we developed a personal development passport?
Within the passport, we have five categories:
How will children use the passport?
Children will be given the opportunity to work towards their passport during curriculum time and in planned enrichment sessions. Achievements will be celebrated via Marvellous Me and during our celebration assemblies when children achieve an activity or experience.
What does this mean at home?
There is no additional workload for parents and carers, just the opportunity to celebrate in your child’s achievements and experiences. As always, if you feel you could support us due to your own experience and / or job role, please get in touch with your child’s class teacher. If you ever achieve one of the passport tasks at home, please share via your child’s dip and do homework book (Years 1 – 6) or via Tapestry (Foundation).
Children will keep their passports in school, in order to keep them safe and to take them with them each year, to the next year group. Passports will always be available at parents evening for you to see.
It could be that with changing cohorts, needs and curriculum, we update the passport from time to time. We will always share these updates with parents and carers.

pageCache.text:
Personal Development
At the heart of our vision is the belief that education should shape the whole child. Our Personal Development curriculum is inclusively planned and sequenced, not just incidental.
Our Personal Development Passports are a cornerstone of this commitment, designed to extend learning beyond the academic and nurture the broader development of every pupil. Through carefully planned experiences, both within and beyond the curriculum, we empower children to explore their interests, discover their talents, and grow in confidence, resilience, and independence. These passports guide pupils on a journey that celebrates diversity, champions fundamental British values, and fosters a deep sense of respect, responsibility, and citizenship. By embedding character education, wellbeing, and community engagement into everyday learning, we ensure our children are not only prepared for future academic success but also equipped to thrive in modern Britain and make a positive contribution to society.
Each year group has a passport of objectives that they work to achieve over the year. All children will be awarded with a passport keepsake badge at the end of each school year which they can collect throughout their duration at Roundwood. Please see how the passport objectives are sequenced below.

Remote Learning
Remote learning statement
In order to continue to provide an ambitious and broad curriculum in all subjects at Roundwood Primary school, where face-to-face sessions cannot be facilitated at school for a prolonged period of time, we will move to remote learning. Remote learning will not be activated for single pupil absence, instead a home learning pack will be issued.
Remote leaning platform
Our remote learning platform is linked to our e-mail provider – Office 365 – Microsoft Teams. Children will use their school e-mail address and password chosen by you. We want to reassure you that the children will not be using the e-mail function it is purely to log in. Whilst these login details have already been shared, if you are having difficulty accessing your child’s account. Please e-mail the school office office@roundwood.bucks.sch.uk who will assist you.
Expected daily / weekly work content
Below details the minimum expectation, in each subject including lesson videos and tasks, of home learning required by each teacher:
Expressive Arts/DT/ Art
Understanding the world/ Geography / History
There is an expectation that all work submitted will have a teacher comment made against it.
Alongside videos and tasks there will be a live weekly assembly for each key stage.

SEND & Inclusion
At Roundwood Primary, we pride ourselves in being an inclusive school, benefitting from experienced staff who have a range of skills and experience in supporting and tailoring learning for children with SEND to ensure all pupil’s flourish.
We identify a child’s individual needs, and their requirements for extra support, through observations, data analysis, consultation with parents and discussions with outside agencies. This is detailed further in our Inclusion Policy and SEND Information Report both of which are available for you to read.
All support provided along with interventions and resources are detailed in an individual learning plan on Edukey which is continually monitored, reviewed and assessed to ensure the additional provision in place is enabling the child to make progress, and regularly adapted to confirm it is current and reflective of the child’s needs. All parents have access to their child's learning plan via an Edukey log in.
Our School SENCO is Ms Laura Tanner, who will happily speak to you regarding any concerns on questions you may have. Please contact her via email ltanner@roundwood.bucks.sch.uk or by telephone on 01280 813066/848306

At Roundwood Primary School, our governors are a dedicated team of volunteers who care deeply about our school and its community. We work closely with school leaders and staff to help shape the school’s future, support progress, and ensure every child gets the best possible start in life.
Governors visit regularly, ask thoughtful questions, and help make sure we’re always moving in the right direction. On this page, you’ll find out who our governors are and their allocated monitoring focus areas. We’re proud of the role our governors play in helping Roundwood thrive.
We’ll be recruiting two new parent governors at the end of this academic year (July 2026). If you're a parent who’s passionate about education and keen to make a difference, we’d love to hear from you.

Curriculum statement
At Roundwood Primary School, we follow the National Curriculum to ensure all pupils benefit from the recognised structure it provides. We have worked hard to personalise topics taught within subjects, as detailed in the NC, to ensure learning is relevant to our school context, environment and fundamentally the needs of our pupils. In order to develop accurate endpoints, we looked at what each pupil would need to know and have experienced in each subject, by the end of their journey with us.
For further guidance, please refer to our curriculum overview documents: How to be successful in each subject.
We understand the importance of having a systemic curriculum in place as it is designed to reduce future gaps, and issues in order to meet endpoints, ensure a suitable transition to secondary school and a sustainable development of society.
We have planned objectives in the form of overarching knowledge that pupils need to know by the end of a unit or topic along with specific vocabulary. Small steps are the measures we adopt to achieve the overarching knowledge. The small steps ensure explicit links are made between reoccurring themes and concepts, skills and knowledge.
Subject leaders determined overarching knowledge from the national curriculum, and devised sequential and logical small steps taking into consideration children’s prior knowledge, environment and endpoints. Teacher’s then assess against the small steps and end points to identify who is on track, and who needs further support, complementing the No Child is Left Behind act.
Leaders at all stages have worked hard to ensure our curriculum is SMART (specific, measurable, attainable, relevant and targeted.)
For further guidance, please refer to our curriculum maps and unit overviews for each subject.
